title: Execution Hypothesis Ledger: Observability-driven Runtime Experiments
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This ledger defines a standard, auditable format for runtime execution hypotheses that are driven by observability signals. It is intended for use when proposing, running, and evaluating small-to-medium scope changes to serving runtime behavior (kernel selection, priority shaping, prefetch hints, eviction policies, and routing fallbacks). The ledger captures hypothesis metadata, preflight checks, telemetry queries, rollout recipes, safety gates, and postmortem templates.

Purpose and scope:

- Purpose: Reduce risk and increase reproducibility for targeted runtime experiments that affect inference economics or latency/fidelity SLOs.
- Scope: Applies to runtime-level experiments owned by eng-serving-runtime, runtime operator interventions by SRE, and paired kernel or scheduler changes authored by kernel-and-scheduling. Not for large-scale model swaps or infra-wide capacity topology changes (those use the Runtime Change RFC process).

Definitions and conventions:

- Hypothesis ID: HYP-YYYYMMDD-N (e.g., HYP-20260201-3).
- Target service(s): runtime-service names as used in our service map (examples: runtime-gateway, runtime-scheduler, kvcache-proxy, kernel-dispatcher).
- Metric windows: we use 5m/1h/24h windows in telemetry queries; specify explicitly.

Hypothesis schema (required fields):

1) id: HYP-...
2) title: short descriptive name
3) owner: primary engineer (email handle)
4) stakeholders: teams impacted (eng-sre, infra, product-ml)
5) background: what observability signal motivated this hypothesis (include link to trace/sample)
6) proposed change: code/config diff references (git commit or config id) and high-level description
7) target_services: list of service names and namespaces
8) expected_outcome: quantitative claim (e.g., reduce p95 latency by 12% at 2k RPS; increase KV cache hit rate from 68% -> 78%)
9) scope: canary percentage, user cohorts, regions
10) duration: planned experiment runtime and measurement windows
11) acceptance_criteria: exact gates (see Safety & Acceptance table below)
12) rollback_criteria: thresholds to trigger immediate rollback
13) observability_queries: list of Prometheus/trace queries used to validate
14) preflight_checks: runbook checklist and SLO impacts
15) approvals: list of approvers and sign-off timestamps
16) artifacts: links to PR, deploy manifest, dashboards, and postmortem template

Experiment lifecycle (step-by-step):

1) Draft hypothesis and attach code PR + telemetry queries. Add to this ledger and notify reviewers.
2) Preflight: run the preflight checklist (below) in staging and obtain approvals.
3) Canary deploy: route 1–5% traffic for 30–60 minutes. Capture full traces and kernel-level histograms.
4) Monitor: automated monitors run checks at 1m cadence; on-call notified if thresholds exceeded.
5) Ramp: if canary is green, increase to 10–30% for 2–4 hours, then to 100% if sustained.
6) Evaluate: run statistical test (see Evaluation method) against control for primary metrics.
7) Decide: Accept, roll forward to prod, or rollback. Document results and close ledger entry with postmortem.

Safety & Acceptance table (copy into PR description):

| Risk vector | Primary metric | Preflight threshold | Canary threshold | Rollback trigger | Owner |
|-------------|----------------|---------------------|------------------|------------------|-------|
| Latency | p95 runtime-gateway (ms) | baseline ± 5% | not worse than baseline + 8% | p95 > baseline + 15% for 5m | eng-sre |
| Error surface | 5xx rate (per minute) | < 0.02% | < 0.05% | > 0.1% sustained 2m | runtime-ops |
| Cost | per-token GPU utilization (%) | n/a | no >10% increase in GC or slots | >20% and forecasted monthly cost delta > 5% | infra |
| Quality | model-output divergence (eval set) | N/A | divergence < configured delta | divergence > configured delta on 50+ samples | product-ml |

Note: thresholds are conservative defaults. The hypothesis owner must explicitly justify any looser gates and obtain signoff from the owners in the Owner column.

Preflight checklist (run before any canary):

- [ ] PR linked and small (single change ideally) with unit tests and CI green.
- [ ] Impacted services identified and owners notified.
- [ ] Replay corpus available that reproduces the observed signal (trace id or synthetic load).
- [ ] Baseline metrics captured for last 72 hours for p50/p95/p99, error rate, queue-length, and KV cache hit rate.
- [ ] Backstop rollout plan documented (how to disable change) and validated on a staging node.
- [ ] Canary dashboards created and templated alerts configured (copy alert rules from this ledger).

Key observability signals to capture (minimum):

- p50/p95/p99 latency per route (runtime-gateway)
- per-kernel execution latency histogram (kernel-dispatcher.kernel.latency_seconds_bucket)
- GPU occupancy and GPU memory headroom (gpu/occupancy, gpu/mem_free_bytes)
- KV cache hit ratio (kvcache.hits / kvcache.requests) and tail latency for cache misses
- Length of the request queue and backlog (runtime-scheduler.queue_length)
- Inference tokens per second and per-request token distribution
- Trace samples showing kernel selection path and dispatch decisions

Automated Prometheus examples (copy-paste):

- p95 runtime gateway (5m window):
  quantile_over_time(0.95, rate(runtime_gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))

- kernel latency histogram (per kernel id):
  sum by (kernel_id) (rate(kernel_dispatch_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]))

- kvcache hit rate (1h):
  (increase(kvcache_hits_total[1h]) / increase(kvcache_requests_total[1h])) * 100

- GPU occupancy spike detector (5m):
  max_over_time(gpu_occupancy_percent[5m]) > 85

Example CLI roll-forward and rollback (internal tooling):

- Create a canary allocation: rwdctl runtime canary create --service runtime-gateway --config git://repo/commit --percent 3 --note "HYP-20260201-3 canary"
- Promote canary: rwdctl runtime canary promote --id canary-123 --to 30
- Abort and rollback: rwdctl runtime canary abort --id canary-123 --reason "p95 regression exceeded threshold"

Evaluation method (statistical):

- Use two-sample bootstrap on aligned request corpus for p95 and mean token cost; require p < 0.05 and effect size > configured min (default 5% for p95).
- Run A/A check prior to A/B to validate sampling system.
- When traffic variability is high, prefer shadowing with mirrored traffic for fidelity checks.

Example ledger entry (text table):

ID: HYP-20260201-3
Title: Adaptive kernel hinting for prefix-heavy workloads
Owner: aisha.patel@redwood.ai
Stakeholders: eng-serving-runtime, eng-sre, applied-ml-and-evals
Background: Observability: 2026-01-29 trace cluster showed repeated kernel cold-path latencies when requests contained long system prompts; KV cache miss tail correlated with specific attention kernel selection. Trace: trace://txn/abcd1234
Proposed change: Add an opt-in kernel hint path that biases dispatch towards low-overhead-gemm for sequences < 512 and switches to high-fidelity kernel only if token entropy > threshold. PR: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/+/789
Target: runtime-scheduler, kernel-dispatcher (namespace=prod-us-east)
Expected outcome: reduce kernel p95 by 10% for prefix length distribution 256–1024, maintain divergence < 0.5% on eval suite
Scope: Canary 3% for 60m, ramp to 25% for 3h if green
Acceptance criteria: see Safety & Acceptance table above
Rollback criteria: p95 regression > baseline + 15% OR 5xx rate > 0.1% sustained 2m
Artifacts: dashboard: /dashboards/hyp-HYP-20260201-3, PR link, replay corpus id: replay/20260201/23

Post-experiment template (to fill after experiment):

- Duration run: start/end timestamps
- Traffic profile: RPS, percent canary, sample entropy distribution
- Observed delta: p50/p95/p99, error-rate, cost delta, kvcache hit delta
- Statistical verdict: pass/fail and p-value for primary metrics
- Lessons learned and recommended followups

Approval and decision matrix:

- Owners listed on the ledger must be notified via #runtime-experiments channel at time of canary start.
- Required approvers before canary: runtime-ops lead, eng-sre oncall, and one applied-ml reviewer if model fidelity is affected.

Conservation of telemetry costs and sampling guidance:

- Prefer stratified sampling: full traces at 3% of requests and aggregated histograms for all requests.
- For long-running experiments, switch to 1m histogram granularity with retained full-trace windows of 15 minutes following alerts.

Appendix A: sample YAML manifest (paste into PR description):

---
# HYP-20260201-3 manifest
hypothesis_id: HYP-20260201-3
owner: aisha.patel@redwood.ai
target_services:
  - runtime-scheduler
  - kernel-dispatcher
canary:
  percent: 3
  duration: 60m
  rollback_criteria:
    p95_regression_percent: 15
    error_rate_threshold: 0.001
observability_queries:
  - "quantile_over_time(0.95, rate(runtime_gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))"
  - "(increase(kvcache_hits_total[1h]) / increase(kvcache_requests_total[1h])) * 100"
---

Appendix B: Ownership contact list (example):

- eng-serving-runtime owner: eng-runtime-lead@redwood.ai (Marco Rinaldi)
- eng-sre oncall: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.ai
- applied-ml reviewer: applied-ml@redwood.ai (Chen Li)

Operational notes and FAQs:

Q: What if canary causes transient kernel noise but metrics return to baseline within 10 minutes?
A: If noise is transient and below rollback thresholds and owner documents rationale, continue monitoring but do not auto-promote. Capture full trace set for later investigation.

Q: Who can override a rollback trigger in emergency?
A: Only the runtime-ops incident commander (IC) with explicit approval from the eng-sre lead; override must be recorded on the ledger entry and later reviewed in postmortem.

Q: How to reference this ledger from a PR?
A: Add a link to this page and include the Hypothesis ID in the PR title and changelog (e.g., "HYP-20260201-3: adaptive-kernel-hinting").

Closeout: Every closed hypothesis must include the artifacts listed above and a one-paragraph summary suitable for the release notes. Major surprises or repeated safety gate trips require a cross-team review and a separate incident review.

Document maintenance: This ledger is maintained by eng-serving-runtime. Additions to thresholds, required telemetry, or approval paths must be proposed via an ADR and reviewed by eng-sre and applied-ml leads.
